General introduction
Biotechnology is a field of study that applies biological knowledge combined with modern technology and techniques to create products for use in human life. Graduates in Biotechnology possess the knowledge and practical skills to delve deeper into and expand their understanding, design, conduct, analyze, and evaluate the results of in-depth experiments in the field of Biotechnology. Simultaneously, with their scientific thinking, logical thinking, critical thinking, and effective work skills, Biotechnology graduates will meet the job requirements in related fields.
The field of Biotechnology has four specialized research areas:
Industrial Biotechnology
Equipping individuals with knowledge of research and production on an industrial scale, applying biotechnology to improve production efficiency, optimize processes, screen and search for new enzyme strains to meet industrial production requirements; researching biological transformation and metabolic products.
Agricultural Biotechnology
Equipping students with the necessary knowledge and skills for human resource development in the agricultural sector, especially in the development of high-tech agriculture, such as micropropagation, plant molecular biology, plant biochemistry, plant interaction, plant pathology, etc.
Medical Biotechnology
The program equips students with general knowledge of medicine and pharmacology, molecular biology techniques applied in the diagnosis of human diseases, research on disease mechanisms, disease transmission mechanisms, and research and development of drug treatments.
Biomaterials technology
Equipping students with the knowledge and skills to develop ideas and conduct clinical trials of biomaterials, fabricate and evaluate biomaterials, isolate and culture cells, and develop nanomaterials, students are given access to equipment specific to the research field.

According to an annual survey conducted by the Department of Biology and Biotechnology with employers, during the recruitment process, most employers focus on the competencies, skills, and attitudes that students have developed after four years of university. At the same time, the majority of employers surveyed indicated little or no discrimination between graduates from Biology and Biotechnology majors when recruiting for positions within their organizations. Furthermore, Biotechnology graduates can now work in hospitals and pursue further studies to obtain professional laboratory testing certifications.

General introduction
Biotechnology is a field of study that applies biological knowledge combined with modern technology and techniques to create products for use in human life. Graduates in Biotechnology possess the knowledge and practical skills to delve deeper into and expand their understanding, design, conduct, analyze, and evaluate the results of in-depth experiments in the field of Biotechnology. Simultaneously, with their scientific thinking, logical thinking, critical thinking, and effective work skills, Biotechnology graduates will meet the job requirements in related fields.
The field of Biotechnology has four specialized research areas:
Industrial Biotechnology
Equipping individuals with knowledge of research and production on an industrial scale, applying biotechnology to improve production efficiency, optimize processes, screen and search for new enzyme strains to meet industrial production requirements; researching biological transformation and metabolic products.
Agricultural Biotechnology
Equipping students with the necessary knowledge and skills for human resource development in the agricultural sector, especially in the development of high-tech agriculture, such as micropropagation, plant molecular biology, plant biochemistry, plant interaction, plant pathology, etc.
Medical Biotechnology
The program equips students with general knowledge of medicine and pharmacology, molecular biology techniques applied in the diagnosis of human diseases, research on disease mechanisms, disease transmission mechanisms, and research and development of drug treatments.
Biomaterials technology
Equipping students with the knowledge and skills to develop ideas and conduct clinical trials of biomaterials, fabricate and evaluate biomaterials, isolate and culture cells, and develop nanomaterials, students are given access to equipment specific to the research field.

General introduction
Biotechnology is a field of study that applies biological knowledge combined with modern technology and techniques to create products for use in human life. Graduates in Biotechnology possess the knowledge and practical skills to delve deeper into and expand their understanding, design, conduct, analyze, and evaluate the results of in-depth experiments in the field of Biotechnology. Simultaneously, with their scientific thinking, logical thinking, critical thinking, and effective work skills, Biotechnology graduates will meet the job requirements in related fields.
The field of Biotechnology has four specialized research areas:
Industrial Biotechnology
Equipping individuals with knowledge of research and production on an industrial scale, applying biotechnology to improve production efficiency, optimize processes, screen and search for new enzyme strains to meet industrial production requirements; researching biological transformation and metabolic products.
Agricultural Biotechnology
Equipping students with the necessary knowledge and skills for human resource development in the agricultural sector, especially in the development of high-tech agriculture, such as micropropagation, plant molecular biology, plant biochemistry, plant interaction, plant pathology, etc.
Medical Biotechnology
The program equips students with general knowledge of medicine and pharmacology, molecular biology techniques applied in the diagnosis of human diseases, research on disease mechanisms, disease transmission mechanisms, and research and development of drug treatments.
Biomaterials technology
Equipping students with the knowledge and skills to develop ideas and conduct clinical trials of biomaterials, fabricate and evaluate biomaterials, isolate and culture cells, and develop nanomaterials, students are given access to equipment specific to the research field.
